spans.s:
hṛd-dhauti
(‘cleansing of the throat’)
------------------------------------------
Haṭhayoga is one of the important branches of योग. It is devoted mainly to the cleansing and the strengthening of the body so that it becomes a fit instrument for the practice of राजयोग.
Dhauti (cleansing process) which is one of the षट्कर्मस् or six practices recommended by हठयोग, is of four types: अन्तर्धौति, दन्तधौति, हृद्-धौति and मूलशोधन.
Hṛd-धौति means cleansing of the throat. It is of three kinds: दण्डधौति, vamana and vastra. As these very names indicate, they are the processes of cleansing the throat passage and oesophagus by using a दण्ड (stick, plantain stalk), by vamana (vomitting) and by vastra (swallowing a thin strip of cloth).
These, however, must be practised under the direct guidance of experts.

hṛdaya
(‘[that which is] taken away [by the sense-objects]’)
------------------------------------------
The word ‘hṛdaya’ is generally used in two senses: the physical heart and the seat of मिन्द्.
It has always been considered as the seat of चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्.
Suśruta describes the shape of the heart as that of a half-open lotus with the face upward.
Caraka (3rd cent. A. D.) says that the ten dhamanīs (ducts) which carry the constituents of the body start from the heart.
Figuratively, the word is used to indicate the inner sense of a thing.
